bracket.note: MOST LIKELY PLAYOFF PATH — a representative bracket built from the simulated seed probabilities and advanced with opponent-conditional win probabilities (higher seed at home, Super Bowl neutral). All playoff/conference/Super Bowl percentages elsewhere come from the full Monte Carlo, which simulates every possible field, matchup and upset.

sb_card.note: most likely pairing from the full matchup distribution; the score is the expected margin around the measured league scoring average

season_detail.game_note: game outcomes shown are the current highest-probability result for each matchup; season record distributions come from all Monte Carlo simulations, never from counting >50% games

season_sim.game_prob_source: stored per-game Monte Carlo p_home where available (current scenario), else power-rating probit from the production game model

calibration.note: calibrated fields (p_playoffs_calibrated, p_division_calibrated) come from the walk-forward-validated Platt correction; raw simulation probabilities remain canonical and are always shown

player_season.method: actual-to-date + per-opponent-adjusted per-game gamma/Poisson x Markov games-played; leaders ranked across joint draws; QB availability discounts pass-catcher efficiency (documented)

movement.note: reasons are the changes recorded between the two runs (finals, refreshes, applied news impacts, retrains, per-team rating/QB input diffs) — movement is never given an invented cause

last_team_sim.game_prob_source: stored per-game Monte Carlo p_home where available (current scenario), else power-rating probit from the production game model

health.status_label: LIVE SEASON SIMULATION · ACTUALS THROUGH 134 FINALS

audit.attribution_source: fresh simulation n=10000 (stored production sim predates divisional tracking)

player_coverage.note: Week-0 analog backtest: 80% season-total intervals under-cover because year-to-year role/usage drift is outside the games-played + per-game-noise model — a documented limitation

confidence.definition: probability = share of simulations where the event happens; confidence = how stable that number is to Monte Carlo sampling, random seeds and rating uncertainty. A probability can be high while confidence is low, and vice versa.
